# One lower point and one point in every exterior cap

Put s=93/1000. Use the six normalized actual contacts

    A=(0,a), B=(b,0), C=(c,0), E=(1,e), F=(f,1), H=(0,h),
    0<a<h<1, 0<b<c<1, a<=e<=h, b<=f<=c.

The four other actual points are P=(p,q), Q=(u,v), R=(r,w), S=(j,k).
Assume every unsigned actual doubled triangle area is at least s.
Here P is inside HABC, Q is in the right cap CE(1,0), R is in the
top cap EF(1,1), and S is in the left cap FH(0,1). These are the
complete N6 exterior count (k,j,r,t,l)=(1,0,1,1,1). Square-side
positions of the free points are allowed. Every chord between actual
points avoids the other actual points because s>0.

**Theorem.** This complete count is impossible at the threshold s.
The proof has two fixed cubic sums, with 324 and 418 positive terms.
Both are printed below. Their geometry and coordinate bounds are
proved first; no feasibility computation is a premise.

## 1. Two exhaustive lower alternatives, with explicit reflection

ONE_LOWER_POINT.md gives two single-ear positions and a central
position for P. The double-ear position is impossible. The square
reflection T(x,y)=(y,x), with the new labels

    A'=T(B), B'=T(A), C'=T(H), E'=T(F), F'=T(E), H'=T(C),
    P'=T(P), Q'=T(S), R'=T(R), S'=T(Q),

preserves this whole count and all normalized contact orders. On the
contacts it sends (a,b,c,e,f,h) to (b,a,h,f,e,c). It interchanges
the two ears and interchanges the quantities ac and bh. Thus exactly
the following two rows suffice, with overlap permitted on ac=bh:

| Row | Lower signs | Additional premise | Lower container floor rho |
|---|---|---|---|
| ear | ACP<0, HBP>0 | none | K s |
| central | ACP>0, HBP>0 | bh>=ac | G s |

Here K=149/20<4+2sqrt(3), G=1457/250<3+2sqrt(2). The lower virtual
endpoint container has doubled area hc. In an ear the two actual
contact-ear areas give hc>=K s, by ONE_LOWER_POINT.md, Section 1.
For the central row the five-point endpoint theorem gives hc>=G s.
The latter theorem also applies in an ear, but the stronger ear
bound is used there. No order between e and f is imposed.

In the central row the same local lemma gives

    hb(c-b)>=s(c+b),
    p>=s(c+b)/(h(c-b)), q>=s(h+a)/(c(h-a)),
    p+q<=1-s/(hc).                                  (1)

The first inequality uses the explicitly chosen weak order bh>=ac.
The other three do not require a contact-order choice.

## 2. Complete initial signs and their finite derivations

Every cyclic triple of ABCEFH has positive orientation. For each free
point, its signs at the six cyclic edges AB,BC,CE,EF,FH,HA are positive
except CEQ, EFR and FHS, which are negative. The remaining initial
region and cross signs are exactly

    HCP<0; HCQ,HCR,HCS>0;
    HEQ<0, HER,HES>0; CFQ,CFR<0, CFS>0;
    HPQ,HPR,HPS>0; CPQ,CPR,CPS<0;
    EQR,FRS,EQS,FQS<0; CQS,HQS>0.                    (2)

Add the two lower signs in the row table. This is the complete initial
sign set; in particular FRS<0 is a uniform cap sign, not a branch.
The first two lines of (2) are the edge and chord tests for the four
stated regions. For the third line, a ray from H to the lower P lies
strictly below HC, whereas its ray to each of Q,R,S lies above HC.
Their positive abscissae give HPQ,HPR,HPS>0. Rays from C give the
three negative signs. Equivalently, expand those determinants using
the two opposite strict HC tests and positive coordinates. The last
line is precisely the six nonnegative-product identities in
N6_CORNER_CONTAINERS.md, Section 5. That proof includes square faces.

Each subsequent line `abcde XYZ sign` in a geometry block applies

    [abc][ade]-[abd][ace]+[abe][acd]=0.               (3)

At that line two products have the same known nonzero sign. The
remaining product has exactly one unknown actual determinant, whose
sign is forced to oppose them. The printed traces give 47 such steps
in the ear and 42 in the central row. They establish every later
containment, convexity and signed factor; no other inference rule is
used in these two traces.

For a positive convex polygon, the inward oriented tests at every
edge establish membership. For a triangle of negative orientation,
all three inward tests have that negative sign. Convexity is checked
by all cyclic triples, so the assertions are explicit finite tests.
Every occupied factor below has its actual occupants printed in its
row's `occupants` block. QS factors display their occupant in the name.

## 3. Rational coordinate bounds

Put

    alpha=1037/10000,
    U=1-s/(1-alpha)=8033/8963,
    V=1-s/U=7199441/8033000,
    L=4s/(1-alpha)=3720/8963.

The actual anchor areas a(c-b), b(h-a)>=s imply a,b>alpha: if the
smaller of a,b were at most alpha, one of these areas would be at most
alpha(1-alpha)=9294631/10^8<s. The projection orders give e,f>=alpha.
The occupied top cap has (1-e)(1-f)>=s, hence e,f<=U and a,b<=U.

The four actual points B,C,Q,E have a nontriangular endpoint hull
inside B,E,(1,0); likewise A,H,S,F inside A,F,(0,1). The four-point
endpoint theorem therefore gives

    e(1-b)>=4s, f(1-a)>=4s,                         (4)

and e,f>=L. Both hull claims follow from the right/left cap tests:
Q is outside BCE and S is outside AFH; the endpoint contacts and the
additional side contact remain extreme. The actual cap clearances
also give e(1-c)>=s and f(1-h)>=s, hence c,h<=V. Consequently

    a,b in [alpha,U], e,f in [L,U], c,h in [rho,V].  (5)

Every free point satisfies (h-a)x>=s and (c-b)y>=s. The simple common
lower coordinate bound is delta0=s/(1-alpha). The cap clearances are

    -[CEQ]=e(u-c)-(1-c)v>=s,
    -[EFR]=(1-e)(r-f)-(1-f)(1-w)>=s,
    -[FHS]=f(k-h)-(1-h)j>=s.                        (6)

Dropping nonnegative terms and coefficients at most one gives the
eight ear-row coordinate lower bounds

    p,q>=delta0; u>=rho+s, v>=delta0;
    r,w>=L+s; j>=delta0, k>=rho+s.

All corresponding upper bounds are 1. Together with (5), this is
exactly the ear initial box printed below.

For the central row set

    delta=s/(V-alpha),
    deltaC=s(V+alpha)/(V(V-alpha)),
    PC=min(V-s/V, 1-s/V^2-deltaC).

The smaller span V-alpha gives the lower bound delta for every free
coordinate. Equation (1), with the monotonicity proved in
ONE_LOWER_POINT.md, Section 4, gives p,q>=deltaC. The HC clearance
bounds each by V-s/V, and its sum bound gives the other bound in PC.
Retaining the coefficients in (6) gives the complete central box

    p,q in [deltaC,PC],
    u in [rho+s/U,1], v in [delta,U-s/(1-rho)],
    r,w in [L+s/(1-L),1],
    j in [delta,U-s/(1-rho)], k in [rho+s/U,1].       (7)

For example e(u-c)>=s gives u>=rho+s/U;
(1-c)(e-v)>=s gives v<=U-s/(1-rho). The top and left bounds follow
from the other forms of (6). Every denominator is positive, as the
exact constants show. The initial box blocks are the exact rational
values of (5)--(7), without a further geometric restriction.

Only the central row then uses interval refinements. Each printed
line gives the factor, target coordinate, old interval, exact feasible
hull, outward new interval, and the full distinct list of endpoint
lines A*x+B. MULTIAFFINE_BOX_BOUNDS.md proves the rule. All its source
factors are physical area or cap inequalities independent of the
coordinate box. In particular no refined-box L factor or box-dependent
support cap is an interval premise. There are 158 displayed steps.

## 4. Basic nonnegative factors

The coordinate order is a,b,c,e,f,h,p,q,u,v,r,w,j,k. In each final
printed box [ell_i,u_i], define L_(2i)=x_i-ell_i and
L_(2i+1)=u_i-x_i. The factors ha,ea,he,fb,cf are respectively
h-a,e-a,h-e,f-b,c-f. A token T_XYZ+ or T_XYZ- is the indicated signed
actual determinant minus s; its sign is established before use.

The other elementary factors are

| Name | Polynomial |
|---|---|
| Vlow | hc-rho |
| TopCount | (1-e)(1-f)-s |
| Right_support | e(1-b)-4s |
| Left_support | f(1-a)-4s |
| low_P | (1-s)/rho-p-q |
| low_sum_P | 1-s/V^2-p-q |
| up_T | x_T+y_T-rho-s, for T=Q,R,S |
| up_weighted_T | V(x_T+y_T)-rho-s, for T=Q,R,S |
| Order_bh | bh-ac, central row only |
| Central_bh | hb(c-b)-s(c+b), central row only |

For low_P, the HC clearance and min(h,c)>=rho give
rho(p+q)<=hc-s<=1-s. The sharper low_sum_P is (1) and hc<=V².
For an upper T, hx_T+cy_T>=hc+s>=rho+s; use h,c<=1 or h,c<=V.
The remaining entries are (1), (4), the occupied top cap, or the
stated contact order.

For Q the factors right_x_Q,right_y_Q,right_px_Q,right_py_Q are

    u-c-s, e-v-s, e(u-c)-s, (1-c)(e-v)-s.

For R the factors top_x_R,top_y_R,top_px_R,top_py_R are

    r-f-s, w-e-s, (1-e)(r-f)-s, (1-f)(w-e)-s.

For S the factors left_x_S,left_y_S,left_px_S,left_py_S are

    f-j-s, k-h-s, (1-h)(f-j)-s, f(k-h)-s.

All follow by dropping nonnegative terms in (6) and using square
bounds. The factors C_XYZ_1 are |[XYZ]|-3s, with one printed actual
occupant. The factors Q_ABCD_1 are [ABC]+[ACD]-(24/5)s, with a
positive convex actual quadrilateral and its printed occupant; the
occupied-quadrilateral theorem permits 24/5<2(1+sqrt(2)).

Only the central row uses four occupied-anchor consequences. With
P inside both ACH and BCH, their areas c(h-a),h(c-b) are at least 3s.
Thus AnchorCap_ACH_0=h-a-3s, AnchorCap_BCH_0=c-b-3s, and

    AH_relative=(1-3s/V²)h-a,
    BC_relative=(1-3s/V²)c-b

are nonnegative. For example c<=V and h<=V imply
h-a>=3s/c>=3sh/V². Every one of these factors has its occupant P
listed; no numerical lower bound is used without its containment.

## 5. Actual support factors and their explicit scalar caps

For a positive convex actual quadrilateral A1B1C1D1 and the actual
occupant P, put X=[A1B1C1], Y=[A1B1D1], Z=[A1C1D1], delta=Y-Z.
Count P in the two contact ears A1C1D1 and B1C1D1. The rates for
counts (0,0),(0,1) or (1,0),(1,1) are 29/5,K,12, respectively, by
QUADRILATERAL_SUPPORT.md. Write the appropriate rate as q0. Then

    QS_A1B1C1D1_P_X = L_X Y-q0*s*delta,
    QS_A1B1C1D1_P_Y = L_Y X-q0*s*delta.              (8)

The affine caps are HCE:h, HCF:c, CEF:1-f, EFH:1-e, ABC:a, ABH:b,
ACH:h-a, BCH:c-b, with 1 for every other actual triangle. These are
proved by direct determinant expansion and the contact orders; their
complete identities also appear in N6_TOP_TRIPLE_SETUP.md, Section 4.
If delta<=0, (8) is nonnegative immediately; if delta>0, the support
theorem gives XY>=q0*s*delta and L_X>=X,L_Y>=Y prove (8).

For a positive convex actual pentagon A1B1C1D1E1, put
X=[A1B1E1], Y=[A1D1E1], Z=[A1B1D1], delta=X-Z. The convex-five
endpoint theorem gives XY>11s*delta when delta>0. Thus

    F5_A1B1C1D1E1_X = Y-11s*delta,
    F5_A1B1C1D1E1_Xbox = B(X)Y-11s*delta,
    F5_A1B1C1D1E1_Ybox = B(Y)X-11s*delta             (9)

are nonnegative; for delta<=0 this follows directly from positivity.
All ten cyclic triples of every printed pentagon are positive in the
preceding trace. No virtual corner is a vertex of these factors.

For a QS suffix Xbox or Ybox, similarly replace the affine L_X or L_Y
in (8) by the scalar B(X) or B(Y). Every such scalar is printed in the
row's `caps` block, with its positively oriented actual triangle word.
Here is an exact formula defining every entry. In the **initial** box,
shift D=[XYZ] by x_i=ell_i+z_i, and expand D=sum d_beta z^beta. Set

    B(D)=min(1, d_0+sum_(beta!=0,d_beta>0)
                    d_beta*product_i(u_i-ell_i)^beta_i, M_D). (10)

The last cap M_D is V for HCE,HCF, 1-L for CEF,EFH, U for ABC,ABH,
V-alpha for ACH,BCH, and 1 otherwise. Its meaning is invariant under
positive cyclic reorderings. These scalar bounds follow from the
same affine caps just listed and (5). The shifted-polynomial bound
in (10) is a finite exact expansion: discard negative nonconstant
terms and bound each positive monomial by its box maximum. It is
an upper bound on D, including on every refined subbox. The explicit
initial endpoints, determinant formula and all exact cap values below
fully specify this calculation. No later refined endpoint is used to
define a cap that would then become its own premise.

## 6. Exact contradictions and whole-count coverage

Every term in each printed sum W is a positive integer times a
product of the preceding nonnegative factors. Therefore W>=0. In
its final printed box, put x_i=ell_i+z_i and expand W=sum c_beta z^beta.
Exactly as in (10),

    W<=c_0+sum_(beta!=0,c_beta>0)
                    c_beta*product_i(u_i-ell_i)^beta_i.       (11)

The displayed rational bound is strictly negative for both sums.
Every product has degree at most 3. There are 324 terms in the ear row
and 418 in the central row, for 742 total; no square or omitted remainder
is needed. The ear row has no interval refinements, and the central
row has 158. Both use continuous rational boxes, including permitted
outer square faces.

Section 1 covers every lower location by an explicit whole-configuration
reflection preserving all three cap counts. The two contradictions
therefore exclude the entire count (1,0,1,1,1), not merely selected
orientations within it. Since s/2=93/2000<A*, this whole family cannot
contain a maximizing configuration at the candidate value.

The companion [check_n6_one_lower_three_caps.py](check_n6_one_lower_three_caps.py)
reads the literal tables, checks every sign deduction, actual occupant,
convex polygon, scalar cap and interval step, then expands both sums
with exact rational arithmetic. This is a transcription aid for the
written identities, not a premise of the proof.
